newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares end 0.65 pct down, await gov't news.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares end 0.65 pct down, await gov't news.

text.p: Istanbul shares dropped amid sharply lower volume on Wednesday as political concerns continued to weigh on prices, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 .XU100 closed at 1,673, down 11 points, or 0.65 percent from Tuesday. It had dived 5.07 percent on Tuesday after soaring 8.04 percent on Monday on political developments.

Trading volume was almost halved to 18.64 trillion lira from Tuesday's 34.42 trillion. Brokers said the market drifted sideways during the day and was likely to continue range-bound trade in the coming days so long as no fresh political news arrived.
The market worries that a coalition planned by Prime Minister-Designate Mesut Yilmaz to exclude the Islamist Welfare, the biggest party in parliament, may not win a confidence vote.

"The market will probably enliven (itself) when Yilmaz presents a cabinet list to the President but will again settle down afterwards to wait for the confidence vote," smail Gner from Info Securities said.
"If Yilmaz gets the vote, then the bourse is likely to exceed its trading record of 1,780," he added.

President Suleyman Demirel appointed conservative opposition leader Yilmaz last week to form a coalition to replace the one-year-old government under Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, who resigned last week under army pressure.
Yilmaz has said he would present Demirel with a cabinet list on June 30.

He has won the backing of two left-wing parties, a secularist small right-wing grouping and conservative independents, but needs the support of around a dozen MPs from rival conservative True Path Party (DYP) to win the vote.
DYP leader Tansu Ciller who allied with Erbakan, has rejected an offer from Yilmaz to join his planned alliance.

* Of the 245 shares traded, 141 declined, 43 advanced and 61 closed steady. The IMKB Industrial dropped 1.37 percent to 1,583, the IMKB Services edged up 0.24 percent to 1,700 and the IMKB Financial slipped 0.22 percent to 1,784.

Leading actives of the day were largely state owned flat steel maker Eregli down 750 lira at 22,250, vehicle maker Otosan, down 2,000 lira 79,000, utilities Cukurova Elektrik unchanged at 240,000 and Aktas Elektrik down 2,500 lira at 230,000. They made up 34 percent of the total turnover.
Otosan's major shareholder Koc group said it would sell a 12.6 percent stake to its foreign partner Ford Motor Co. as part of their late 1996 agreement to equalise their stakes in the joint venture.
